decisions.reason: The source-selection and production-scope changes in message 179 are already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; the duration change requires no additional edits.
The complete-moment criteria and expanded production contexts from message 179 are already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
Message 179 specifies complete standalone content units, which are owned by REQ_COMPLETE_TEACHING_MOMENT; it does not necessarily change this candidate's separate strong-moment selection standard.
The new duration range and platform contexts do not state or necessarily imply any change to caption color, font, or effects.
Message 179 does not restate or extend the clean-editing, effects, or transition requirements; shared Family membership is insufficient for propagation.
The message reiterates personal client approval and approved-only quota counting, but these rules are already present and the duration modification does not change them.
The only new quota detail in message 179, the roughly 3-4-clips-per-day cadence, is already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; the duration change adds nothing further.
The welcome and growth language does not alter the existing Lead Clipper pathway, responsibilities, compensation, or training state.
The statement that the freelancer is hired does not modify the historical qualification method, and implementation or completion status must not be propagated as a requirement-state MODIFY.
Message 179 does not change the project-chat submission channel or the task-local sample-review workflow.

Creating clips for Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and TikTok does not necessarily require the freelancer to publish to all three; the message only promises an assigned Instagram account, so the existing publishing destination remains unchanged.
